sourced_facts: Eqs1-2 define a normalized Gibbs binary law with unary terms and an unrestricted function of total count.
Eq4 and page4 restrict recursive cardinality subsets to nested or disjoint sets; arbitrary potentials at their counts include unary factors.
Eqs6-7 introduce deterministic sum-count auxiliary variables without changing the binary law.
§5.2 messages are exact convolutions; §5.2.3 states O(D log² D) time and O(D log D) space for balanced FFT trees, with O(D²) worst-case time for unbalanced trees.
§5.3 samples root counts then child count splits and leaves to draw exact joint configurations.
source_conclusion.overlap: Structured count supervision, proper count-dependent joint binary laws and exact marginal/sampling inference are established.
source_conclusion.proposal_adaptation: Use a visible-context conditional two-sided count potential over native NCNC residual slots and label-only TRAIN observation bits; serve structural draws through one shared nonlinear decoder.
source_conclusion.complexity_boundary: Arbitrary cross-side g(K_L,K_R) is not a unary potential on a single union count. It requires the separately stated full count-grid work; the paper fast bound is not claimed for that model.

source_conclusion.verified_title: Stochastic Multiple Choice Learning for Training Diverse Deep Ensembles
source_conclusion.saved_takeaway: The oracle objective sums each example's minimum member loss. Each minibatch forwards all members and backpropagates an example only through its minimum-loss member. Expertise emerges from winner-take-gradient training; top-k winner variants interpolate toward ordinary ensembles.
source_conclusion.attributed_prior_vs_open_gap: Credit training-time assignment, stochastic block gradient descent and specialization. A TRAIN-topology partition would change the assignment criterion and can add a common competence anchor; it does not discover specialist training or block routing.
source_conclusion.closest_capable_comparator_role: Closest newly read learning-operation ancestor. A loss-based assignment adaptation with the same shared/private routing, normalization, anchor and uniform serving isolates whether graph-conditioned assignment adds utility. This adaptation is not a native sMCL reproduction.
source_conclusion.limitations: Oracle accuracy is a different served objective from uniform mean prediction. No source implementation, proof or numerical reproduction read. Its image/segmentation/captioning results cannot be used as graph quality evidence.
source_conclusion.decisive_next_step: Use as attributed scope/control evidence; no native port or scientific launch adopted by this packet.

The reverse step factorizes over nodes/edges conditional on the current noisy graph; that next graph is fed back through repeated learned transitions.
Shared graph-transformer context combines node, edge and global features; dense layers have quadratic node-pair work.
§4.2 and Appendix B add noisy/visible-graph structural and spectral descriptors; Appendix B notes cubic spectral work on the small graphs used there.
